summary: Christopher Key Chapple is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).
Christopher L. Diamond works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Heidi R. M. Pauwels (~2013–2018) and held a post at the Australian National University (~2020).

Christopher Minkowski is an Indologist who studied at Harvard College, the University of Delhi, and Harvard University. He held positions at Brown University, the University of Iowa, Cornell University (1989–2006), and Oxford University as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney works in Indology and history/archaeology. His career includes posts at the Australian National University (~1993–1995), University College London (professor from ~1995), the University of Chicago (~2000–2001), Northwestern University (~2008), the University of Cape Town, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Christopher S. George is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler, Geshe Wangyal, and Padma Gyaltsan. He founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972) and taught at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions.

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held posts at Harvard University (~1989–2016) as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on the Study of Religion and World Religions.

Christopher Wallis works in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from the University of Rochester, the University of Oxford (studying under Alexis Sanderson), and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt, later serving as a guest lecturer at Naropa University.

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He held teaching posts at the University of Nanking (1943–1947), the University of Iowa (~1955–1966), and the University of Kansas (from 1966).

Chuan-ying Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and sinology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, studying under Chu-tsing Li, John Hay, and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield.
Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor (attested 2015) and former professor (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.

Chun-fang Yu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Columbia University, as well as under traditional teachers Nanting and Sheng Yen. She held posts at Rutgers University (attested 2000) and Columbia University (professor, attested 2007–2015; emerita attested 2026).

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University and National Central University under Shuming Liang, Shili Xiong, and Thomé H. Fang. He held posts at National Central University (1944–1949), the New Asia Institute (~1953–1978), and CUHK (~1963–1974).

Chun-min Yen works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Yen earned a PhD at the University of Arizona, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert M. Gimello, teacher Todd Brown, and traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.

Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies figure who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, Shechen Kongtrul, and at Oxford. He was a spiritual advisor at Young Lamas Home School (1959–1963) and founded Naropa University (1973).
Chökyi Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Khakyab Dorje, and taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Lama Ngawang Zangpo.

Clara Sue Kidwell was a historian who earned her master's and PhD at the University of Oklahoma. She held positions at Haskell Indian Nations University, UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian, the University of Oklahoma, and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

Clare Carlisle is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002). She held posts as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and professor at King's College London (~2020).

Linguist Claude Hagège studied at ENS, ENLOV, and under André Martinet. His posts include CNRS (~1965–1970), the University of Poitiers (1970–1987), EPHE (~1970–1982), Paris 12, Paris-Sorbonne, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and the Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques was an Indologist and historian who studied under George Cœdès. He served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient and taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1998).
